question.problem: Consider the equation $\operatorname{sin}⁡(2x+{30}^{∘})=-\frac{1}{2}$ for ${0}^{∘}\le x<{360}^{∘}.$ If the solutions ${x}_{1},{x}_{2},{x}_{3},{x}_{4}$ are written in ascending order, what is the numerical value of ${x}_{2}\cdot {x}_{3}?$
question.worked_solution:
We will find the general solution to the equation, and then generate all of the solutions in the required domain.

The general solution to our equation is

$$
\begin{aligned}2x+{30}^{∘} & =-{30}^{∘}+n\cdot {360}^{∘}, & \, & \, & 2x+{30}^{∘} & ={210}^{∘}+n\cdot {360}^{∘}.\end{aligned}
$$

Solving the two equations above for $x$ gives:

$$
\begin{aligned}2x & =-{60}^{∘}+n\cdot {360}^{∘} & \, & \, & 2x & ={180}^{∘}+n\cdot {360}^{∘} \\ x & =-{30}^{∘}+n\cdot {180}^{∘} & \, & \, & x & ={90}^{∘}+n\cdot {180}^{∘}\end{aligned}
$$

We set $n=0,\pm 1,\pm 2,…,$ until we have generated all solutions in the domain ${0}^{∘}\le x<{360}^{∘}.$

- Setting $n=0$ gives $x=-{30}^{∘}$ and $x={90}^{∘}$

- Setting $n=1$ gives $x={150}^{∘}$  and $x={270}^{∘}$

- Setting $n=2$ gives $x={330}^{∘}$  and $x={450}^{∘}$

All other values of $n$ generate solutions outside the domain ${0}^{∘}\le x<{360}^{∘}.$ So, the solutions ${x}_{1},{x}_{2},{x}_{3},{x}_{4}$ (written in ascending order) are

$$
x={90}^{∘},{150}^{∘},{270}^{∘},{330}^{∘}.
$$

Finally, since ${x}_{2}={150}^{∘}$ and ${x}_{3}={270}^{∘},$ we have

$$
{x}_{2}\cdot {x}_{3}=150\cdot 270=40\,500.
$$
